name: Well-differentiated Papillary Mesothelial Tumour of the Peritoneum
aliases: Well-differentiated Papillary Mesothelioma of the Peritoneum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for WDPM

criteria.description: Presence of well-differentiated papillary structures lined by bland mesothelial cells without stromal invasion
Positive immunostaining for mesothelial markers such as calretinin, WT-1, and cytokeratin 5/6
No evidence of stromal or deep tissue invasion on histology
Presentation with peritoneal nodules or plaques without significant symptoms or systemic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of well-differentiated papillary mesothelial proliferation with positive immunohistochemical markers and absence of stromal invasion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of malignant mesothelioma and other papillary peritoneal lesions.

pathognomonic.notes: Often discovered during imaging or surgery for unrelated reasons
searchTerms: small abdominal nodules found by chance

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated papillary peritoneal lesions without invasion

common.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to peritoneal involvement
common.notes: May result from localized fluid accumulation
searchTerms: abdominal bloating due to peritoneal issues

common.notes: Non-specific symptom related to peritoneal irritation
Usually minimal compared to malignant mesothelioma
searchTerms: small amount of fluid in abdomen

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to peritoneal irritation

rare.notes: Very rare, due to mass effect

searchTerms: fluid in chest from abdominal leak
pleural effusion caused by peritoneal-pleural connection

rare.notes: Very rare and not well characterized

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated CA-125 levels
imaging: CT scan showing multiple well-defined peritoneal nodules without invasion
MRI demonstrating papillary peritoneal lesions with no deep tissue infiltration
Ultrasound may reveal small peritoneal masses or ascites
genetic: No recurrent genetic mutations identified; differs from malignant mesothelioma genetic profile
other: Histopathology showing papillary architecture with bland mesothelial cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for calretinin, WT-1, cytokeratin 5/6

distinguishingFeatures: Higher mitotic activity and cellular atypia
Epithelial origin with different immunohistochemical profile
More aggressive behavior and poor prognosis

redFlags: Evidence of stromal invasion on biopsy
Significant weight loss and systemic symptoms
